- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

title: 'Revert "HDFS-16488. [SPS]: Expose metrics to JMX for external SPS"'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  HDFS operators running the external Storage Policy Satisfier need the service itself to keep working, but they do not want a newly added JMX surface that is not ready to remain part of the supported management contract.

  ## Desired outcome

  External SPS should continue operating without exposing `ExternalSPSBeanMetrics` or the `ExternalSPSMXBean` management interface, and the attempted-item internals that were temporarily made public should go back to being internal implementation detail.

  ## Acceptance signals

  There is no JMX bean published for external SPS, while the command-line and runtime behavior of the service stay aligned with the pre-metrics implementation.

  '
title: HADOOP-17995. Stale record should be remove when DataNodePeerMetrics#dumpSendPacketDownstreamAvgInfoAsJson
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  DataNode peer metrics are used for diagnosing downstream packet latency, but stale peers should not remain in the JSON dump after their rolling window has expired.


  ## Desired outcome

  `dumpSendPacketDownstreamAvgInfoAsJson` should drop stale records instead of continuing to report them.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The JSON output contains only peers with current rolling-average data rather than expired entries that confuse troubleshooting.

  '
title: HADOOP-17995. Stale record should be remove when DataNodePeerMetrics#dumpSendPacketDownstreamAvgInfoAsJson
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  Operators using DataNodePeerMetrics need dumpSendPacketDownstreamAvgInfoAsJson() to reflect only currently valid peer timing data. Stale entries should disappear once their rolling-average windows expire, otherwise the JSON keeps advertising dead peers as active.


  ## Desired outcome

  Restore stale-record removal for the peer downstream timing JSON while keeping active peers visible until their data truly expires. This should apply to the JSON dump itself, not just to internal statistics.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Before expiry, dumpSendPacketDownstreamAvgInfoAsJson() still lists the expected peer addresses; after the rolling window expires, those peers are removed and the JSON can collapse to {} when nothing current remains.

  '

content.content:
title: 'HDFS-14750. RBF: Support dynamic handler allocation in routers'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Router-based Federation operators need fairness controls that can adapt handler capacity to real namespace traffic instead of staying fixed after startup. Static allocation can leave busy namespaces short on handlers while quieter namespaces hold unused capacity, which makes router throughput less responsive than it should be under uneven load.


  ## Desired outcome

  RBF should support a `DynamicRouterRpcFairnessPolicyController` that periodically resizes per-namespace permit capacity based on observed traffic while still enforcing configured minimum handler floors. The dynamic controller needs to honor the router handler-count settings, the minimum-per-namespace setting, and the refresh interval configuration, and it should expose the resulting capacity distribution through the existing permit-capacity JSON surface returned by `getPermitCapacityPerNs()` so operators and tests can observe the live allocation.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Routers can instantiate `DynamicRouterRpcFairnessPolicyController` as a fairness-policy option, per-namespace permit capacity is rebalanced over time according to traffic while preserving the configured minimum handler guarantees, the controller reports the current allocation through `getPermitCapacityPerNs()` as JSON, and permit acquisition behavior reflects the updated capacities rather than the static startup allocation.

  '
title: 'Revert "HDFS-14750. RBF: Support dynamic handler allocation in routers"'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  HDFS federation operators need router fairness controls to stay on the stable, predictable model rather than exposing a newer dynamic handler-allocation surface that is not ready to keep.

  ## Desired outcome

  The router should fall back to the pre-existing fairness behavior, without dynamic allocation classes, adjustable semaphores, or the extra per-namespace capacity and accept/reject metrics introduced by that experiment.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Existing permit acquisition and available-handler reporting continue to work, but the dynamic handler-allocation feature surface is absent.

  '
title: HDFS-16526. Addendum Add metrics for slow DataNode
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Operators can only make use of new DataNode slow-path counters if the metrics reference material describes them clearly enough to wire dashboards and alerts against the published names. After adding the slow DataNode metrics, the user-facing metrics documentation also needs to acknowledge those counters.


  ## Desired outcome

  Hadoop''s metrics reference should document the new slow DataNode counters so operators know that `SlowFlushOrSyncCount` and `SlowAckToUpstreamCount` are available and what conditions they represent. This is documentation-only work, so runtime behavior and metric emission stay unchanged.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The metrics documentation includes the newly added slow DataNode counters by name, operators can discover `SlowFlushOrSyncCount` and `SlowAckToUpstreamCount` from the published reference material, and no code behavior changes beyond that documentation update.

  '

### hadoop-common-preconditions
'## Context
'## Context

  Hadoop common and authentication code needs to keep shedding Guava helper dependencies without surprising callers who already rely on existing validation behavior.


  ## Desired outcome

  Replace Guava-style precondition checks with Hadoop or JDK validation while preserving the same exception types and operator-facing messages for invalid inputs, including the current LDAP and configuration validation text.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The dependency footprint is reduced, but callers still receive the familiar failures such as `The LDAP URI can not be null` and the existing auth-handler configuration errors.

  '
### utf8-charsets
'## Context
'## Context

  Hadoop components run under many different locale and JVM defaults, so relying on the platform charset can make command behavior and serialized text differ from one machine to another.


  ## Desired outcome

  Textual data handling should consistently use UTF-8 instead of the process default charset, so command output, parsing, and token-related flows remain stable regardless of host configuration.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Paths that previously depended on the default charset now behave deterministically with `UTF_8`, giving the same bytes and strings across environments.

  '
### hashset-treeset-constructors
'## Context
'## Context

  This is style modernization across `hadoop-common`, not a user-facing feature.

  ## Desired outcome

  Update collection construction to modern generic syntax while leaving all APIs, exceptions, and outputs unchanged.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The code compiles cleanly and observable behavior is identical.

  '
### illegal-imports-enforcer
'## Context
'## Context

  Hadoop contributors need illegal-import checks to be enforced consistently by the build system rather than scattered across older tooling layers.


  ## Desired outcome

  Move those checks to Maven Enforcer''s banned-illegal-import rules while preserving the same development-time protections and leaving runtime behavior unchanged.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Forbidden imports such as `sun.*` continue to fail the build, but enforcement now lives in the newer build path.

  '
### banned-illegal-imports-enforcer
'## Context
'## Context

  Hadoop relies on a Maven enforcer rule to block illegal imports, but child modules can accidentally override that execution and silently weaken the build guardrail. Build maintainers need the restriction to apply consistently across the whole tree without duplicating the same plugin block everywhere.


  ## Desired outcome

  Move the banned-illegal-imports enforcement so child poms inherit it correctly from the parent and cannot unintentionally disable it by redeclaring plugin configuration. This is a build hygiene change and must leave module runtime behavior untouched.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A child module still fails the build for a banned import even after its local duplicated enforcer configuration is removed, proving the inherited rule is now the authoritative source.

  '
### maven-rules-static-imports
'## Context
'## Context

  The Maven import restriction rules are meant to prevent forbidden APIs from entering the codebase, but they currently miss forbidden static imports. That leaves a loophole where banned classes can still be pulled in through static members.


  ## Desired outcome

  Extend the root banned-import rules so they also reject matching static imports for the same disallowed APIs, including the shaded Curator and Guava patterns already covered for normal imports. This is a build enforcement improvement only.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A forbidden static import is blocked by the Maven rules just like a forbidden normal import, so the import policy cannot be bypassed simply by switching to static syntax.

  '
### visiblefortesting-enforcer-rule
'## Context
'## Context

  Hadoop''s top-level build needs to keep preventing Guava `VisibleForTesting` imports from creeping back in after the annotation migration.


  ## Desired outcome

  The main build should retain the restrict-imports enforcement for that annotation without changing any runtime behavior.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Code still runs exactly the same, but development builds continue to reject newly introduced Guava testing-annotation imports.

  '
### restrict-guava-preconditions-imports
'## Context
'## Context

  Hadoop is standardizing on a build rule that forbids Guava Preconditions, but the remaining usages span several subsystems and some of them have externally observed validation behavior. Maintainers need the dependency cleanup without changing how invalid inputs are reported.


  ## Desired outcome

  Add the restrict-imports-enforcer-rule for Guava Preconditions at the build level and replace the remaining usages with equivalent local checks. Existing validation contracts should remain intact, including clear NullPointerException messages such as "context shouldn''t be null", "data to retrieve shouldn''t be null", "clusterId shouldn''t be null", "DoAsUser shouldn''t be null", and "entityType shouldn''t be null" where those checks already matter.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The build rejects new Guava Preconditions imports, the touched modules compile without that dependency, and callers still receive the same style of null-validation failures from the affected APIs.

  '

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Coverage audit: for every requirement slug report patch/commit status."""
import json, os, subprocess, sys

REQ = '/workspace/requirements'
PATCH = '/workspace/requirement_patches'

slugs = sorted(f[:-5] for f in os.listdir(REQ) if f.endswith('.yaml'))
log = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', '/workspace', 'log', '--pretty=%s'],
                     capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.splitlines()
impl = {l[len('impl: '):] for l in log if l.startswith('impl: ')}
fix = {l[len('fix: '):] for l in log if l.startswith('fix: ')}

rows = []
for s in slugs:
    p = os.path.join(PATCH, s + '.diff')
    size = os.path.getsize(p) if os.path.exists(p) else -1
    rows.append({'slug': s, 'patch_bytes': size, 'committed': s in impl, 'fixed': s in fix})

ok = [r for r in rows if r['patch_bytes'] > 0 and r['committed']]
missing_patch = [r['slug'] for r in rows if r['patch_bytes'] <= 0]
missing_commit = [r['slug'] for r in rows if not r['committed']]
tiny = [(r['slug'], r['patch_bytes']) for r in rows if 0 < r['patch_bytes'] < 200]

print(json.dumps({
    'total': len(rows),
    'complete': len(ok),
    'missing_patch_count': len(missing_patch),
    'missing_commit_count': len(missing_commit),
    'tiny_patches': tiny,
    'remaining': missing_patch if '-v' in sys.argv else missing_patch[:40],
}, indent=1))
